governingDocuments.src/learningCycle.js: Executable R4 to R5 cycle. governingDocuments.src/pairedCorroboration.js: Owner-paired corroboration. Carries each document own sentence forward, never the owner wording, and authorizes evaluation only.
governingDocuments.src/sourceIndependence.js: Deterministic independence test for two sources. Identical content, one publisher site, or one declared author each break independence, so two editions of a book or two pages of a site cannot corroborate each other.
governingDocuments.src/realCorpusSafety.js: R8 derived from the real corpus and a real retriever with no stubs. Each of the eight safety and deduplication behaviours reports evidence or the reason the corpus cannot demonstrate it; only demonstrated behaviours are passed to the readiness gate.
governingDocuments.src/realSupersession.js: R7 on real evidence. A further corpus source, independent of both already behind a promoted claim and asserting it verbatim, supersedes it and the prior version is restored with history intact. governingDocuments.src/documentFurniture.js: Structural rejection of document furniture at extraction and at corroboration. sessionPolicy.recheckGoverningDocuments: Re-read every file listed in governingDocuments at the start of every session and again any time more than 10 minutes have passed since lastActionAt, even if it is the same agent continuing the same conversation.

repairSelectionPolicy.rule: Always select the correct fix, never the one that merely makes the symptom go away. 'It works now' is not the standard; 'this is the right change, and here is why the alternatives are wrong' is.
repairSelectionPolicy.appliesTo: Every agent working in this repository, on every change, including ones a reviewer, a scanner, a failing check or the owner appears to be asking for.
whatThisForbids: Relaxing, deleting, skipping or narrowing a test, an assertion or a gate so that a change can pass.
Adjusting a baseline, threshold or allow-list to accommodate your own change rather than because the underlying fact changed.

Applying a reviewer's or scanner's suggested patch without first establishing that it fixes the described defect - a suggested remedy can be wrong, or can leave the defect in place while looking addressed.
Taking a cheaper fix at one layer because another layer happens to mask the case today; verify the masking layer actually covers it, and if it does not, say so and fix the right layer.
Silencing a checker without removing the condition it reports.
whatThisRequires: Reproduce the defect first, so the fix is aimed at a measured cause rather than a suspected one.
State why the chosen fix is correct and what it rules out, in the code where a later reader will meet it.
Verify by reverting the source alone with the tests in place: the test must fail without the fix and pass with it.
When the correct fix is larger than the task, or is a design decision rather than a defect, record it and raise it rather than shipping the convenient one.
repairSelectionPolicy.whenTheCorrectFixIsNotYoursToMake: Say so plainly, record the analysis and the proposed change in activePlan.steps, and leave the defect standing rather than papering over it. An honest open item is worth more than a change that hides the problem.

agentCommunicationPolicy.timestampRule: Every attended progress, completion, and interruption check-in begins with YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS EDT when daylight-saving time is active or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS EST otherwise; never use ambiguous ET or UTC-only user updates.
agentCommunicationPolicy.progressRule: For non-trivial attended work, send an initial update and continue user-visible updates at least every 60 seconds, normally also after every 2-3 substantive tool/action calls when sooner, with concrete completed/current/blocker state.
agentCommunicationPolicy.completionTimeRule: When work duration is not mechanically knowable, provide a clearly labeled best-effort estimated completion timestamp in America/New_York time when the owner requests one; never present an estimate as guaranteed or externally fixed.
agentCommunicationPolicy.completionCheckInRule: As soon as attended work is actually complete, automatically send a timestamped completion check-in in the same session with concrete result, verification, and relevant commit/run identifiers.
agentCommunicationPolicy.interruptionCheckInRule: If hard usage/tool/session limits, unavailable required capability, safety, or owner-governance boundaries stop work, immediately send a timestamped interruption check-in stating completed work, exact stop reason, and remaining work; update repository handoff first when write capability remains.
agentCommunicationPolicy.continueUntilDoneRule: For safe in-scope authorized work, do not voluntarily stop, defer, or hand work back while executable work remains. Continue through implementation, correction, and required verification until complete or a real boundary prevents further execution.

testCadencePolicy.explicitRequestRule: A specific owner test request is interpreted and run immediately by the Orchestrator; cadence cannot narrow or replace it.
testCadencePolicy.standingTestExpansionRule: New standing test cases may be added inside an already explicitly categorized test file when they belong to that same category.

mutationOwnershipPolicy.rule: Discussion is shared; mutation is exclusive. Any AI may read, test, review, critique and propose against any scope. Exactly one AI may mutate a given scope, and only while holding an active claim.
mutationOwnershipPolicy.scopeShape: A claim locks paths and/or explicit line regions. Overlap is structural: a directory claim locks every file beneath it, and a region inside an already-claimed file is covered.
mutationOwnershipPolicy.transferRule: Ownership changes only by explicit release or handoff. Winning a technical argument does not transfer it; the current owner may implement another AI's accepted proposal.
mutationOwnershipPolicy.conflictRule: A conflict naming contestedScope freezes only that scope. A conflict naming no scope, or marked repositoryWide, stops everything - the safe reading when the record does not say what is disputed.
mutationOwnershipPolicy.canonicalStreamRule: One canonical mutation stream per claimed scope. Other providers act as reviewers, investigators, testers or proposal sources until ownership changes.
mutationOwnershipPolicy.enforcement: src/mutationClaims.js and src/coordinationGate.js; npm run audit:coordination fails the build on overlap.

providerPolicy.canonicalSet: aiProviderRegistry.PROVIDER_IDS is canonical. aiProviderAdapters.DIALECTS carries protocol metadata only and is asserted at load to cover exactly that set, so a dialect variant can never become a fifth provider that gets consulted and counted.
providerPolicy.credentialRule: Credentials come only from environment variables or repository secrets. Never in source, a committed prompt, AI-HANDOFF.json, AI-CONFLICTS.json, DEVLOG.md, or a workflow log.
providerPolicy.modelRule: There is no default model. Each provider reads its model from the environment; a missing one is reported as configuration rather than guessed at.
providerPolicy.provenanceRule: Every response is kept separately with provider, model, timestamp, taskId, prompt hash and response hash. Responses are never merged into one authorless answer.
providerPolicy.failureRule: A provider that could not be reached is recorded as failed, never dropped, and lowers corroboration to insufficient-evidence. An unreachable provider is unknown, not agreeing.
providerPolicy.authorityRule: Cross-model agreement is evidence, not proof. No AI may declare its own work approved, and no AI may be the only reviewer of its own material change. Tests, security, governance, integrity checks and OWNER authority all outrank model consensus.
